## make a simple regression model

```{r}
bears <- read.csv(file="BEARS.csv",header = TRUE)
#adjust factors to be factors
bears$SEX<- as.factor(bears$SEX)
bears$MONTH<- as.factor(bears$MONTH)
```

## Model LENGTH ~ NECK  this is an example  

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~NECK,data=bears, pch=17)
```

As neck circumference increases, length tends to increase.  

Compare all models that predict LENGTH other than NECK.  
Then order them from worst to best by its value of Adjusted-Rsquared (bigger is better), or by RSE (residual standard error) where smaller is better. 

```{r}
model.1 <- lm(LENGTH~NECK,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.1)
```
The adjusted R squared is 0.7476

## Model LENGTH ~ HEADLEN

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~ HEADLEN,data=bears, pch=17)
```

As the head length increases it gets bigger.  

```{r}
model.2 <- lm(LENGTH~HEADLEN,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.2)
```
adjusted R-squared is 0.8434

## Model LENGTH ~ HEADWTH

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~ HEADWTH,data=bears, pch=17)
```

As head circumference increases, length also rises on the chart 

```{r}
model.3 <- lm(LENGTH~HEADWTH,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.3)
```
Adjusted R-Squared is 0.5321,  making it the smallest number in the ranking.

## Model LENGTH ~ CHEST

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~ CHEST,data=bears, pch=17)
```

As chest of bear gets bigger, so does the length. 

```{r}
model.4 <- lm(LENGTH~CHEST,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.4)
```
adjusted R-squared is 0.7869

## Model LENGTH ~ WEIGHT

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~ WEIGHT,data=bears, pch=17)
```
As weight increases in the bear, making the length of the bear long.   

```{r}
model.5 <- lm(LENGTH~WEIGHT,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.5)
```
Adjusted R-squared is 0.7423. 

##FINAL RANK  

LENGTH~HEADLEN -0.8434     
LENGTH~CHEST - 0.7869    
LENGTH~NECK - 0.7476    
LENGTH~WEIGTH- 0.7423    
LENGTH~HEADWTH - 0.5321
